newsitem.title: USA: Third incinerator lawsuit filed against Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Third incinerator lawsuit filed against Illinois.

text.p: A third lawsuit challenging Illinois repeal of a state subsidy for waste-to-energy incinerators has been filed in Madison County Circuit Court.
James Stamos, a Chicago attorney representing Polsky Energy Corp., said Monday the suit was filed against various Illinois officials earlier this month.

The lawsuit claims the repealed subsidy violated the contract clauses of the state and U.S. constitutions in connection with an incinerator project Polsky was planning in Wood River, an Illinois town near St. Louis.

Stamos said the project had received all necessary state approvals and that Northbrook, Ill.-based Polsky had expended millions of dollars based on the receipt of those approvals. While a bond issue had been planned for the scrap wood and tire burning incinerator, no debt had been sold at the time the subsidy was repealed, he added.
Rick Redmond, a Chicago attorney representing the state, said he was aware the lawsuit had been filed, but had not yet received a copy of it.

The lawsuit followed two others that were filed by developers of incinerators in Robbins, Ford Heights and Fulton in the wake of Gov. Jim Edgar's signing into law in March a bill repealing the subsidy.

Nearly $500 million of unrated tax-exempt bonds were sold to finance those three projects, which were largely dependent on selling the electricity they produced to utilities at a higher rate subsidized by the state.

On Nov. 1, U.S. District Court judge in Chicago dismissed a lawsuit brought by Foster Wheeler Corp., the developer of the Robbins facility. An executive at the Clinton, N.J.-based company has said the dismissal would be appealed in the U.S. Court of Appeals, while the company also considers filing another lawsuit in state court and seeking administrative relief state agencies.

Another lawsuit, filed by CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton, the developers of bond-financed incinerators in those two towns, is partially pending in Cook County Circuit Court. In September, a judge dismissed bondholders from the lawsuit. The judge also dismissed part of the developers' lawsuit against state of Illinois officials.
Attorneys representing the state have filed a motion to dismiss the remainder of the lawsuit, which challenges the legality of the retroactive removal of the state subsidy for incinerators.
